clue.text: Put rug on the table!

parts.note: to put something is to place it
a mat is a small rug

explanation.surface: An odd domestic order to lay a carpet across the dining table.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue both builds the answer and describes it: a small mat set at each diner's spot on the table.
explanation.definitionFit: A small mat laid under each diner's plate is a rug of sorts for the table.

clue.text: Heartless prig hurried during crash

indicators.note: one piece occurs during the other, so it sits inside it
a word with its heart removed keeps only its first and last letters, here of prig

parts.note: hurried means ran

explanation.surface: A callous prude rushes off just as there is a collision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' keeps only the outer letters of prig, and 'during' sets the running inside them. PRANG is British slang for a minor car or plane crash.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a collision, usually of a car or aircraft.

clue.text: Inferior inexpensive card

parts.note: inexpensive means cheap
the jack is a playing card

explanation.surface: A low-quality bargain playing card.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective it means shoddy, of poor quality, like a pedlar's wares.

clue.text: Man with Italian drink

parts.note: Martin is a man's name

explanation.surface: A fellow accompanied by someone from Italy, perhaps sharing a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A cocktail of gin or vodka with vermouth.

clue.text: Irritation one could get whilst pruning roses

definitions.text: Irritation one could get whilst pruning roses

parts.words: Irritation one could get whilst pruning roses
parts.note: literally a prickle lodged in the gardener's skin; figuratively a constant source of annoyance

explanation.surface: A gardener complains of a hazard of cutting back rose bushes.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a persistent annoyance, just as a spike stuck under the skin is.

clue.text: Flowery lady starts languishing

parts.note: Flora is a woman's name

indicators.note: the start of languishing gives its first letter

explanation.surface: A lady with a fondness for blossom begins to wilt.
explanation.definitionFit: Floral and flowery are synonyms, both meaning decorated with or relating to blooms.

clue.text: Beefier hash supplied for nothing

indicators.note: a hash is a jumbled mess, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A meatier stew is handed out without charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hash' looks like the food but signals the anagram of BEEFIER.
explanation.definitionFit: A gift given free of charge, something one receives without paying.

clue.text: Turn over cover on desk

parts.note: to turn over is to roll
a top is a cover or lid

explanation.surface: Flip the lid that sits on a writing table.
explanation.definitionFit: A type of writing bureau with a flexible slatted lid that slides up.

clue.text: From which to see the capital?

definitions.text: From which to see the capital?

parts.words: From which to see the capital?
parts.note: a viewing point over the city, cryptically an organ of sight belonging to the capital itself

explanation.surface: A question about the best vantage point for viewing the city.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital is London, and its big observation wheel on the Thames is named as the city's eye.
explanation.definitionFit: The giant observation wheel on London's South Bank gives views over the city.

clue.text: A soft fruit to become visible

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical abbreviation for soft
a pear is a fruit

explanation.surface: A gentle piece of produce starts to show itself.
explanation.definitionFit: To come into view is to show up, the same as emerging.

clue.text: Plain diagram with no partitions

parts.note: plain in the sense of frank or unconcealed means open
a plan is a diagram

explanation.surface: A simple drawing shows a layout without internal walls.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes an office or home layout without dividing walls between areas.

clue.text: Initiative needed to stick small part I can get on

parts.note: to gum is to stick
pt is the abbreviation for part

explanation.surface: Enterprise is required to glue down a small piece one can manage.
explanation.definitionFit: Gumption is resourcefulness and common sense, the drive to act on one's own.

clue.text: Orbits round bar

indicators.note: turned round, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something circles a drinking establishment.
explanation.definitionFit: A small restaurant or wine bar.

clue.text: North American may, these days, accompany Scottish man

parts.note: may in the sense of being permitted means can
AD (anno domini) is the current era
Ian is a typically Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: Someone from across the Atlantic may join a Scot in modern times.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Canada, a country in the northern part of the American continent.

clue.text: It is what ferries do with what is left

definitions.meaning: a remainder taken forward to the next period

explanation.definitionFit: Ferries transport people across, and a balance taken forward to the next account is a remainder.

clue.text: One during restless sleep to slip away

indicators.note: the piece comes during the other, placed inside it
a restless sleeper moves about, so these letters are shuffled

parts.note: a means one

explanation.surface: Someone, during a disturbed night, drifts off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restless' shuffles SLEEP to ELPSE and 'during' sets A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Time that passes or goes by without notice.

clue.text: Car driver George

parts.note: auto is short for automobile, a car
a pilot drives an aircraft

explanation.surface: A motorist named George.
explanation.walkthrough: 'George' looks like a man's name but is pilots' slang for an automatic flight control system.
explanation.definitionFit: Airmen's slang nickname for the device that steers a plane automatically.

clue.text: Stern rebuke for astronauts?

definitions.meaning: the vehicle that carries astronauts into space

explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a severe reprimand, and the vehicle that launches crews into space.

clue.text: Likely to depreciate

parts.note: depreciate in its sense of belittle, describing someone inclined to disparage others' motives

explanation.definitionFit: A sceptic who assumes the worst of others readily belittles them.

clue.text: Became tardier having done this

parts.note: someone who lingered ends up later; the word is also an anagram of tardier

explanation.surface: A remark about falling further behind after lingering.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of TARDIER rearranged give the answer, and dawdling would indeed make you later.
explanation.definitionFit: Delayed or lingered, which makes one later than before.

clue.text: It comes to the ones who succeed

definitions.text: It comes to the ones who succeed

parts.words: It comes to the ones who succeed
parts.note: succeed in the sense of following on, as heirs do, rather than achieving success

explanation.surface: A motivational saying about rewards going to the successful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'succeed' means coming after someone, as heirs do, not winning.
explanation.definitionFit: An inheritance passes to the descendants who follow on.

clue.text: Tracks lira fluctuation using established routine

indicators.note: a currency's fluctuation changes it, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a way is a manner or established practice

explanation.surface: Monitors the Italian currency's movements by habitual method.
explanation.definitionFit: A line of rails on which trains run.

clue.text: Over there did not start bone-dry concoction

indicators.note: a concoction is a mixture, so these letters are blended
the word loses its opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone yonder failed to begin a very dry mix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'did not start' removes the B from BONEDRY, and 'concoction' rearranges ONEDRY.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned way of saying at a distance, in that place.

clue.text: There is no cheating in it producing beautiful scenes

definitions.text: There is no cheating in it

parts.note: fair means beautiful, as in a fair maiden
a play is made up of scenes

explanation.surface: A production with lovely sets has nothing underhand about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Honest conduct in a game, keeping to the rules.

clue.text: Petty officer trapped by one animal or another

indicators.note: the officer is caught inside the other piece

parts.note: a yak is a Tibetan ox

explanation.surface: A naval officer is caught by some creature or other.
explanation.walkthrough: The YAPOK is the water opossum of South America.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition stands for a second creature, a South American water opossum.

clue.text: Is outspoken before Ella starts to sing

parts.note: being vocal means being outspoken

indicators.note: the start of Ella gives its first letter

explanation.surface: A frank remark is made before Ella Fitzgerald begins her song.
explanation.definitionFit: To vocalise is to use the voice in song, especially on vowels.

clue.text: Beer, prisoner brought back the whole lot inside

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other
something brought back is reversed in direction

parts.note: POW is a prisoner of war
all means the whole lot

explanation.surface: A captive returns with all the ale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' reverses the prisoner of war abbreviation, and 'inside' puts the whole lot within it. WALLOP is British slang for beer.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for beer or ale.

clue.text: Put film in camera for at least the second time

definitions.text: Put film in camera for at least the second time

parts.words: Put film in camera for at least the second time
parts.note: loading a camera once more, i.e. doing it again

explanation.definitionFit: To load again means filling the camera with film a further time.

clue.text: Needle's hiding-place?

parts.note: alludes to the saying about searching for a needle in a pile of dried grass

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom says looking for a needle in one is near impossible, so it is a fine hiding place.
